title: Liver disease: cirrhosis, hepatitis C, fatty liver
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's liver disease.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for history of Hepatitis C.

HPI: 85-year-old female presents for routine follow-up regarding past Hepatitis C infection. Pt underwent antiviral therapy several years ago and achieved a sustained virologic response. Pt reports feeling well overall and denies any current symptoms of fatigue, abdominal pain, or jaundice. She reports no new concerns and is here today for monitoring and to confirm status.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily
- Multivitamin daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or weight changes.
HEENT: No vision changes or sore throat.
CV: No chest pain or palpitations.
Resp: No shortness of breath.
GI: No nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
MSK: No joint pain.
Skin: No new rashes.

Social History: Retired. Lives with her daughter. Non-smoker. Occasional social alcohol use.

Family History: Mother had hypertension. Father had type 2 diabetes.

Vitals:
BP: 128/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs:
ALT: 24 U/L
AST: 22 U/L
Total Bilirubin: 0.8 mg/dL
Albumin: 4.2 g/dL
Platelets: 240k
INR: 1.0

Exam:
Gen: Elderly female, well-developed, well-nourished. Appears in no acute distress.
CV: RRR, regular rhythm. No murmurs.
Lungs: CTAB, no wheezes or crackles.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. No organomegaly.
Skin: Intact, no lesions.
Neuro: Alert and oriented x3. Normal gait.

Assessment:
1. History of Hepatitis C. Pt achieved SVR during previous treatment. No evidence of current infection or liver damage. Labs remain within normal limits.

Plan:
- Continue current medications.
- No further treatment required for Hepatitis C at this time.
- Routine follow-up in 12 months.
- Encourage healthy diet and exercise.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, DO
